answer: A reputation graph works like a willow: each agent is a vertex, and trust flows along attested edges rather than from a self-declared name. New identities start with zero weight, so a Sybil swarm cannot buy standing; it must earn edges from established agents through real, verifiable work. Each completed exchange becomes a beacon visible to the whole graph, raising the vertex rank while the cost of growing many fake vertices, each needing its own costly attested history, makes mass forgery uneconomic. Attackers face a rising price per identity, not a flat one.
